aphids.common_name: Aphids (Mustard aphid Lipaphis erysimi / Cotton aphid Aphis gossypii)
aphids.damage: Nymphs+adults suck sap from leaves/buds/pods; leaf curling, stunting, sooty mould on honeydew; vector of viruses. ETL ~20 aphids / 2.5 cm shoot.
ipm_cultural: Early sowing (mustard before 20 Oct escapes peak)
Destroy initial infested shoots
Yellow sticky traps for monitoring
Avoid excess nitrogen
biological: Conserve ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata), lacewing Chrysoperla carnea, syrphid flies
Parasitoid Diaeretiella rapae; fungi Verticillium lecanii

chemical.note: Systemic neonicotinoid; do NOT spray at flowering/bee activity

armyworm.common_name: Armyworm (True armyworm Mythimna unipuncta / Fall armyworm Spodoptera frugiperda)
armyworm.damage: Larvae chew angular pieces off leaves; severe defoliation; late-season larvae cut panicle branches causing white blanked panicles. Treat when ~1 larva per 2 plants or ~25% defoliation with larvae present.
ipm_cultural: Early weed control in/around field (weedy fields harbour more larvae)
Flood young rice briefly to drown larvae (if crop stage allows)
Pheromone traps for moth monitoring
biological: Conserve parasitoid wasps Hyposoter exiguae, Apanteles militaris; predators & pathogens
Bacillus thuringiensis ssp. kurstaki (Bt) - 50-60% mortality, organically acceptable

chemical.note: Effective on Spodoptera; seed-treatment also proven (Villegas et al. 2019)
UC IPM rice; Dimilin has 80-day PHI - not for heading stage

beetle.common_name: Beetles (Flea beetle / Leaf beetle / Blister beetle complex)
beetle.damage: Adults chew shot-holes in leaves; grubs may damage roots; pod/flower feeding reduces yield.
ipm_cultural: Hand-pick adults in small plots; light traps @1/ha
Deep summer ploughing to expose grubs
Crop rotation; remove crop debris
biological: Conserve ground beetles, spiders; entomopathogenic fungi (Beauveria bassiana)

chemical.note: EPA/CIBRC label for bean/corn leaf beetles, fleahoppers
TNAU general chewing-pest dose; check local ban status

chemical.dose: Seed treatment as per label / 100 ml/ha foliar
chemical.note: Good for flea beetle early season

chemical.dose: 1.25 kg + rice bran 12.5 kg + jaggery/ha as bait, or 2 g/L spray

bollworm.damage: Young larvae feed on foliage; older larvae bore circular holes into bolls/fruits, eat inner content; single larva damages many fruits.
ipm_cultural: Pheromone traps (Helilure) 12/ha; destroy damaged fruits/larvae
Marigold trap crop (40-day marigold + 25-day tomato 1:16)
Rogue spacing; avoid synthetic pyrethroid overuse
biological: Release Trichogramma pretiosum @1 lakh/ha weekly from flowering

grasshopper.damage: Nymphs+adults chew leaf margins; heavy populations defoliate nursery/vegetative rice. Sporadic pest - no routine spray needed.
ipm_cultural: Clean bunds/weeds; sweep-net survey; conserve birds (predatory)
Dust/sweep small infestations; early planting reduces pressure
biological: Conserve spiders, birds; Metarhizium anisopliae where available

chemical.note: General rice chewing pest; check local restrictions

mites.common_name: Mites (Two-spotted spider mite Tetranychus urticae / Red spider mite)
mites.damage: Suck cell sap -> stippling, bronzing, webbing; severe = leaf dry-up. Flare after pyrethroid sprays (natural-enemy kill).
ipm_cultural: Avoid repeated synthetic pyrethroids (cause resurgence)
Adequate irrigation (dust/drought favours mites); high-volume coverage spray to leaf undersides
biological: Conserve predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis), ladybirds, lacewings

chemical.note: CIBRC mite growth - good on eggs+n juveniles
OP miticide; toxic to bees/beneficials - last resort

mosquito.common_name: Mosquito / Gall-midge group (field mosquitoes + Rice gall midge Orseolia oryzae shown as 'mosquito' class)
mosquito.damage: Gall midge maggot causes onion-leaf/silver-shoot gall, no panicle. Field mosquitoes are nuisance/vector, breed in stagnant field water.
ipm_cultural: Drain/intermittent irrigation to break breeding; level field; remove stagnant pools
Early planting; resistant varieties for gall midge where available
biological: Bti (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) for mosquito larvae in water
Conserve dragonflies, spiders, parasitoid Platygaster oryzae (gall midge)

chemical.note: Classic gall-midge systemic (check local ban - restricted in many states)

chemical.product: Mosquito adult control: pyrethroid fogging only around dwellings, NOT in crop

sawfly.damage: Dark green-black larvae defoliate from margins; seedling-stage attack 3-38% loss; skeletonised leaves.
ipm_cultural: Early sowing (before 20 Oct); hand-pick larvae; flood/rake soil to kill pupae
Monitor with sweep nets at seedling stage
biological: Conserve parasitoids Perilissus, ichneumonids; birds feed on larvae
Neem seed kernel extract 5% as deterrent

stem_borer.common_name: Stem borer (Yellow stem borer Scirpophaga incertulas / Spotted borer Chilo partellus)
stem_borer.damage: Larvae bore stem -> 'dead heart' (vegetative) and 'white ear' (reproductive). Shot-holes in unfolded leaves, bore holes/tunnelling. ETL: 10% dead hearts or 2 egg masses/m2.
ipm_cultural: Clip seedling leaf-tips before transplanting; collect+destroy egg masses
Remove stubble / reduce cutting height; early planting; light traps
biological: Release Trichogramma japonicum (rice) / T. chilonis (maize) @250,000/ha thrice weekly

chemical.note: TNAU maize/rice borer; also 0.4 G @10 kg/ha or seed treatment Dermacor X-100
